To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The amount of polymer adsorption at the solid liquid interface increases with the rate of macromolecular supply to the surface.

(i) the amount of polymer sorbed at the solid-liquid interface depends on the rate of polymer delivery, (ii) the rate dependence is due to conformational relaxation of adsorbed polymer, and (iii) the amount of adsorbed polyanion is determined by the excluded area effect.

the area occupied by an adsorbed polycation is 1.6 times larger than the area of its projection onto a flat surface, the area increases by 0.3% per hour of polymer supply, and the area increases by about 1% per hour of structural relaxation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the combined effects of the excluded area of macromolecules at the interface and the relaxation of the macromolecules themselves on the adsorbed amount of polyelectrolys.
the effect of structural relaxation of adsorbed macromolecules on the amount of polyeleotrolyte adsorbed at solid/liquid interface.
the adsorption of polyelectroylte on solid surfaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structural relaxation of macroions at a solid-liquid interface is a very complex and not yet well understood process.
structural relaxation and excluded volume are important in determining adsorption at solid liquid interfaces.
the structural relaxation and the excluded area are the two most important factors in the determination of the amount of polyelectroylte adsorbed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adsorbed amount of polymer at a solid liquid interphase is determined by the competition between the excluded volume effects and the conformational relaxation of macromolecule.
the adsorption of a polyelectrolys at a solid/liquid interface is a dynamic process.
the excluded area is a function of both time and the number of adsorbed macromolecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of confor- mational relaxation, the amount of polymer sorbed at the solid liquid interface is a function of the rate of polymer adsorption.

the excluded area is an important factor in the determination of the adsorbed amount of polyelectrolys and that the area occupied by the polymer is not constant but depends on the time elapsed from the start of the adsorption process.
the area occupied by a single macromolecule increases with time and reaches a limiting value, which depends on the rate of polymer delivery and the rate of structural reorganization.
